subject: Request for deterministic throughput window / dedicated capacity addendum — Arctica Systems
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@arctica.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Elliott <tom.elliot@arctica.com>, procurement@arctica.com
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deterministic throughput window for trading hours

Hi David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the Dedicated plan, our trading platform has a very tight two-hour market-open window (09:30–11:30 ET) where tail latency spikes are unacceptable. We need to understand whether Redwood can guarantee deterministic throughput and queue isolation during that period. Specific asks: 
- A throughput guarantee (tokens/sec or requests/min) backed by credits if missed
- Reserved GPU count that prevents preemption by background/maintenance traffic
- Behavior of queueing when headroom is exhausted (do requests get queued, dropped, or degraded?)

Attached a small sample of our production traffic (anonymized). Can we get a proposed addendum or playbook that maps to our operational constraints?

Best,
Sofia
Senior Infra Engineer, Arctica Systems
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@arctica.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deterministic throughput window for trading hours

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the sample traffic. High-level response: we can offer a time-sliced deterministic reservation for the open window combined with a soft priority queue for non-window traffic. Summary of what we propose today (see attached draft addendum):

- Dedicated reservation: 8 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent) for 09:30–11:30 ET with isolated scheduling tokens
- Throughput target: 95k tokens/min aggregate (measured at ingress) for the window; objective is 99.9% of 1-minute intervals
- Fallback behavior: if transient oversubscription occurs we will scale into burst capacity (if purchased) or apply preconfigured graceful degradation (lower quantization level + response trimming) before dropping requests
- Queueing: requests in the window are placed into a priority isolation queue with a maximum enqueue latency of 250ms; beyond that threshold requests are returned with a 503 + backoff_hint.

Ben and I will align on commercial terms; Irene, can you validate the runtime implications and confirm whether warm-start KV cache is needed to meet the 250ms enqueue target for Arctica's payload pattern?

I'll follow up with a redline-ready addendum.

Thanks,
David
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@arctica.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deterministic throughput window for trading hours

Sofia —

Quick commercial note while we circle on tech: the suggested reserved 8-GPU block + priority reservation maps to our Dedicated Tier 2 pricing. I put a preliminary term sheet into HubSpot (link below) with a proposed monthly commit and a throughput credit schedule for SLA misses (credits accrue as % of monthly invoice). High-level options:

- Option A (Standard): 8 reserved GPUs, burst pool optional, 12-month term
- Option B (Committed): 12 reserved GPUs, higher headroom, 24-month term, deeper discounts

If you want I can turn the draft addendum into a DocuSign-ready attachment once the tech redlines are in.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/48391/ARC-2028-0191

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@arctica.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deterministic throughput window for trading hours

David / Ben —

Reviewed the traffic sample and did a quick capacity sketch. Notes: 

- Warm KV cache is strongly recommended for Arctica's request patterns (high repetition of prompt prefixes). We should include a pre-warm step (30 min before market open) and a short steady-state warm window (first 10 minutes) in the runbook.
- Isolation tokens + priority queues will require a small scheduler delta; estimated impact on platform: +6% CPU on the scheduler plane and a negligible increase to GPU utilization variance.
- Enqueue latency guarantee (250ms) is feasible if we enforce a per-tenant request cap at ingress and run autorepair on slow instances aggressively. If Arctica expects request bursts >3x baseline, we should move to Option B or add burst credits.

I've attached a short technical appendix to the draft addendum with runbook steps, warming commands, and expected monitoring signals (headroom, enqueue_depth, cache_hit_rate).

Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Elliott <tom.elliot@arctica.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deterministic throughput window for trading hours

David / Ben / Irene —

Thanks for the quick turn. The proposed approach looks promising and aligns with our expectations. A couple of follow-ups before we get legal involved: 

1) Can you change the SLA clause to show credits on a per-minute aggregation (so we don't get hit by noise from single-second spikes)?
2) We need confirmation that maintenance events will not overlap the 09:30–11:30 reserved window without 72h advance notice and a mitigation plan.
3) Please redact any internal scheduler metrics from the public runbook — we just need the steps and observable signals, not raw operational counters.

We'll review the draft addendum and send redlines by Friday. If you can prepare a DocuSign-ready version next week that includes Option A pricing, that would help procurement move quickly.

Best,
Tom
Director of Platform Engineering, Arctica Systems
